name: SEIS Long Development Roadmap
principles: one reversible slice at a time
public experience and governance evolve together
runtime dependencies stay unchanged until a decision record approves them
remote publishing waits for verified GitHub authentication and branch state
accessibility and reduced-motion behavior remain non-negotiable

phases.label: Foundation hardening
phases.intent: Keep the current static shell, development process, and quality gates coherent.
phases.proof: check:foundation and roadmap checks pass without heavy builds

phases.label: Experience expansion
phases.intent: Turn the public shell into a richer lab surface without increasing cognitive load.
phases.proof: UI stays readable across mobile and desktop with reduced motion enabled

phases.label: Content intelligence
phases.intent: Give artworks, case studies, and lab operations stronger editorial metadata.
phases.proof: content registries validate before any framework migration

phases.label: Operations and server readiness
phases.intent: Prepare live upload only after server target and GitHub auth are confirmed.
phases.proof: UIXAppTTR is the only remote branch and deploy target values are explicit

phases.label: Framework decision
phases.intent: Choose a future app framework only when static constraints become limiting.
phases.proof: migration is justified by maintainability, not hype or visual ambition

phases.label: Release system maturity
phases.intent: Make package, backup, upload, and recovery flows boring, observable, and repeatable.
phases.proof: release can be prepared, checked, restored, and explained from docs

nextLongRunActions.title: Build the roadmap surface into the static app
Create a manual accessibility review checklist
Model case study detail pages before choosing a framework
Resolve GitHub auth and remote branch cleanup outside runtime changes
